subtitle: Meatball soup with mint
verso: With its rice and its mint so green, the best albóndiga you've ever seen.
story: Mexican meatballs carry raw rice inside, which swells as they cook and keeps them tender, and fresh mint, which is the flavor everyone remembers.

ingredients.title: Meatballs
items: ¼ cup long-grain rice, soaked 15 minutes in hot water and drained
1 tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper

ingredients.title: Broth
items: 8 cups beef or chicken broth (or water)

steps: Mix all the meatball ingredients with your hands just until combined. Wet your hands and roll balls the size of a golf ball.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and chipotle. Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the purée 5 minutes, until it darkens.
Add the broth and the mint sprig. Bring to a boil and add the carrots and potato.
Lower in the meatballs one at a time. Don't stir for the first 10 minutes so they can set.
Simmer 25–30 minutes, adding the zucchini for the last 10. Taste for salt.

pressureCooker.time: 8 min high pressure + 10 min natural release
steps: On Sauté, fry the tomato purée 5 minutes.
Add the broth, mint, carrots and potato. Gently set in the meatballs.
Add the zucchini and simmer on Sauté 3 minutes.

tips: Some families tuck a piece of hard-boiled egg inside each meatball. Kids love finding it.
Keep your hands wet while rolling and the meat won't stick.
